game.title: Grand Theft Auto VI
game.setting: Leonida — Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Mount Kalaga, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and the Grassrivers
game.difficultyRating: 4/10 — the list asks for stamina and tidiness, not reflexes; almost nothing on it can be failed outright

roadmap.title: Phase 1 — The Campaign
roadmap.tagline: Lucia and Jason, end to end
roadmap.brief: Run the story first and hunt nothing on the side. Missions open the state district by district, teach the systems every later phase leans on, and pay out twelve trophies just for reaching the credits. At each chapter break, park a manual save in its own slot and never overwrite it: two trophies on this list turn on single story moments, and a save from just before them is the cheapest insurance the whole hunt offers.
roadmap.focus: Clear every chapter and named mission; bank one untouched save per chapter break.

roadmap.title: Phase 2 — Strangers of Leonida
roadmap.tagline: Six strands that ripen while you wait
roadmap.brief: Stranger strands arrive in instalments: a meeting, a pause measured in in-game days, then a new marker. Open every strand the hour its marker appears and let the pauses run in the background of other phases, so the waiting costs you nothing. Each finished strand also feeds the silver Strangers & Freaks tally, which wants eight completions across the state, so no strand is ever a detour.
roadmap.focus: Open all strands early; close Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone.

roadmap.title: Phase 3 — Activities & Medals
roadmap.tagline: Sample everything, then master the range
roadmap.brief: With the map open, tour the activity icons once each — that single lap earns Master of None and shows you which activities you actually enjoy. Then settle into the scored ones: shooting-range golds, drone races at every site, twenty race wins. These trophies reward repetition on short loops, so they fill dead time between strand instalments better than anything else in the mid-game.
roadmap.focus: One lap of every activity type; golds at the range; a drone win at each location.

roadmap.title: Phase 4 — Exploration
roadmap.brief: Exploration pays for curiosity with a map open beside you. Sweep Leonida region by region for the meditation spots, the vehicle discoveries and the full-map reveal, and register cars to the Scooter Bros app as they cross your path. Do this phase while your story knowledge of the map is fresh: places you visited once for a mission are twice as fast to sweep now as they will be in a month.
roadmap.focus: All meditation spots; 100 vehicles discovered; the whole map uncovered.

roadmap.title: Phase 5 — Combat & Crime
roadmap.tagline: Plan the getaway before the grab
roadmap.brief: The crime trophies are scored on escapes, not entries. Scout each target in daylight, park a fast car facing the exit, and only then go loud — or, for Sneakthief, never go loud at all. Bank vaults, armored trucks, gang operations and the showroom classic all follow the same rhythm: quiet preparation, thirty loud seconds, a rehearsed drive into the Grassrivers or the Keys until the stars blink out.
roadmap.focus: Five bank vaults; one operation per gang; the jewelry store taken silently.

roadmap.title: Phase 6 — Partner Work
roadmap.brief: Three trophies need Lucia and Jason together, and all three are easier inside a single deliberate session than scattered across a playthrough. Bring both characters to the same neighbourhood, work the wanted-level escape first while you are fresh, then the three-shop robbery chain, and let Personal Best happen naturally while the two are travelling together between the set pieces.
roadmap.focus: Lose four stars together; rob three shops back-to-back; keep the pair together.

roadmap.title: Phase 7 — The Long Counters
roadmap.brief: What remains is arithmetic: 250 stunts, three card sets, 100 WAiNK spots, 50 challenges, a quarter-million laundered and every garage bought. None of it is hard and all of it is long, which is why the hunt rules had you starting these counters in Phase 1. Work from the in-game stats screen, clear one counter at a time, and let the 100% checklist be the last thing standing between you and the platinum pair.
roadmap.focus: Finish counters from the stats screen; close out 100% completion last.

roadmap.title: Phase 8 — The Platinum Pair
roadmap.brief: Two trophies close the hunt and neither has a trick to it. A Long Road pays at 100% completion on the in-game checklist — not at the end of this guide's list, but at the end of the game's own accounting. Vice Got a Price! then awards itself the moment the other fifty-four are all earned. If one counter disagrees with this page, believe the game's screen and go find the missing item.
roadmap.focus: Drive the in-game checklist to 100%; the platinum follows on its own.

rules.title: Keep three rolling saves
rules.text: One save sits before each chapter's point of no return, one is your current free-roam save, and one is a cold backup you touch only when something goes wrong. The list's two missable trophies both turn on single moments; with a chapter-break save behind you, a missed moment costs a reload instead of a second playthrough.

rules.title: Start counters on day one
rules.text: Stunts, collectible cards, WAiNK spots, laundered bills and shop spending all accumulate quietly while you play the story. Glance at the stats screen once per session and spend ten minutes on whichever counter is lagging. A counter started in hour one finishes itself; a counter started in hour eighty is a grind you chose.

rules.title: Strands before story's end
rules.text: Open every stranger strand the moment its marker appears, even if you cannot finish it yet. Strands advance on in-game days, and several need long pauses between instalments. A strand opened in Chapter 2 ripens while you play; a strand opened after the credits makes you wait around for content you could have had for free.

rules.title: Plan the escape before the crime
rules.text: Every robbery trophy is decided by the getaway. Before you touch a vault, a truck or a gang operation, scout the block, park a fast car facing the way out, and know which bridge, causeway or swamp track you will take when the stars arrive. Thirty seconds of preparation is worth five minutes of improvised fleeing.

rules.title: Partner trophies in one session
rules.text: The three partner trophies all need both protagonists in the same place at the same time, and the setup is the fiddly part. Do them together in one sitting: bring Lucia and Jason to the same district, run the wanted-level escape, then the shop chain, and let togetherness trophies tick while you travel between the two.

rules.title: The game wins every argument
rules.text: This guide is written against the official trophy list and Rockstar's published material, and it will occasionally be wrong about the shipped game — a count, a location, a label. When the page and the game disagree, the game is right. The stats screen and the 100% checklist are the final authority on everything they measure.

faq.q: Can anything on this list be missed permanently?
faq.a: Two trophies can be missed on a single pass: Actions Speak Louder, which turns on a story choice, and Bad Luck, I Guess, which needs you to fail once and then succeed. Both are safe if you keep the chapter-break saves described in the rules — reload, choose or play it the other way, and continue. Everything else on the list stays available after the credits.

faq.q: How long is the platinum, honestly?
faq.a: Budget 85 to 110 hours. The story is roughly a third of that; the counters are the rest. The estimate assumes you start the long counters during the campaign, as the roadmap suggests. A hunter who leaves stunts, cards and laundering until the endgame should expect the top of the range, and a second partial playthrough for a missed trophy adds ten hours or more.

No trophy on the official list is tied to a difficulty setting, and nothing in the list rewards playing above the default. Play on the setting you enjoy. The handful of genuinely demanding items — the shooting-range golds, the silent jewelry robbery — are about preparation and routing, not about enemy health pools.

faq.q: What should I do first on a fresh save?
faq.a: Play the opening, then make your first manual save the moment free roam opens, and start glancing at the stats screen early so the counters become familiar. Open stranger strands as their markers appear, try activities as you pass them, and keep one save per chapter break. The roadmap's order does the rest — nothing in Phase 1 needs hunting for its own sake.

faq.q: Do I need GTA Online for any of these?
faq.a: No. All 55 trophies are earned in the single-player game, including the partner trophies — the partner is the other protagonist, not another player. You can complete the entire list offline once the game is installed, which is also how this guide's tracker is designed to work: everything happens on the page, in your browser.

faq.q: The tracker lost my ticks — what happened?
faq.a: Ticks live in your browser's local storage for this page, so clearing site data, switching browsers or using a private window will empty them. Export your progress from the tracker bar before any of those, and import the file afterwards. The export is a small JSON list of trophy ids — nothing else about your play is stored or sent anywhere.
